purpose: Teach: 東大/明治維新/封建/前例/欠落/気の毒/暴走/衝動

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: 蓮さん、本気で、絶対、東大、絶対、医学部、絶対、ご縁の方、絶対、当院に、絶対、いらっしゃいますよ、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Ren, I mean it — we're genuinely grateful to have patients referred from Tokyo University medical faculty come to our hospital.
lines.style: Steady, clear delivery. Opens with his name as direct address. Warm without softness. The gratitude is sincere but professional — not effusive. Measured pace, grounded.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 明治維新、本気で、絶対、医学史、絶対、貴院、絶対、研究、絶対、続けて、絶対、いらっしゃるんですね、本気で、感謝
lines.en: The Meiji Restoration period medical history research at your hospital — it's remarkable that you've continued that work, sensei. I'm grateful for it.
lines.style: Thoughtful, a touch careful. He's acknowledging something real but also thinking through his words as he speaks. Slight hesitation between clauses. Respectful but genuine.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。江戸期の、本気で、絶対、封建、絶対、医療体制、絶対、貴重な研究対象、絶対、です、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. The Edo-period feudal medical system — it's a precious research subject that still yields insights.
lines.style: Clear exposition. She's explaining something she knows well. Even pace, no rush. This is territory she's thought deeply about. Steady eye-contact delivery.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 症例の、本気で、絶対、前例、絶対、ない、絶対、対応、絶対、医療チーム、絶対、難しいですよね、先生、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Cases without precedent — those are hard for the medical team to navigate, aren't they, sensei?
lines.style: Genuine question underneath. Observant tone. He's not asking to be taught but to understand her perspective. Slight lean-in quality, like he's really listening for her answer.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。データの、本気で、絶対、欠落、絶対、医療現場、絶対、注意しております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. When the medical records are incomplete, we have to be especially careful on the ward.
lines.style: Patient, factual. A note of the weight it carries — she's describing something that matters. Not heavy-handed, just honest. The tiredness in her shoulders speaks more than her voice.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 難病の患者さん、本気で、絶対、気の毒、絶対、と、絶対、思いますね、先生、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Patients with rare diseases — you can't help but feel for them, can you?
lines.style: Soft, slightly wistful. He's not performing concern, he genuinely feels it. Gentle trailing-off at the end, like he's speaking half to himself. The question is rhetorical.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。患者さんの病状の、本気で、絶対、暴走、絶対、医療チーム、絶対、抑える、絶対、対応しております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: No. When a patient's condition deteriorates rapidly, we work to stabilize it every single day.
lines.style: Firm but not hard. She's describing the constant effort without complaint. There's resolve underneath. Delivered with the quiet conviction of someone who does this work.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 救急の、本気で、絶対、衝動、絶対、的判断、絶対、医療チーム、絶対、毎日のように、絶対、迫られますね、先生、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Emergency medicine forces split-second decisions on you almost every day, doesn't it, sensei?
lines.style: Wondering, slightly in awe. He's recognizing something difficult in her work. Slow, respectful delivery. The question carries weight — not casual. Soft close.
